rules.title: Not X but Y
rules.guidance: State the actual positive claim directly when the negative half adds no information; review split-sentence contrasts and clipped negative tails too.
rules.exceptions: Retain a supported correction of an actual reader belief, necessary statistical contrast, negation, or two informative alternatives. Do not remove an exclusion or change the comparator.

rules.title: One-line closers and dramatic fragments
rules.guidance: Review short restating paragraphs, repeated closers, fragment sequences and dramatic emphasis. Merge or remove only a redundant statement; retain every new fact or consequence.
rules.exceptions: A short sentence with a new empirical result, clinical warning, mathematical definition, or real consequence is useful; uppercase scientific acronyms are not dramatic emphasis.

rules.title: Sayings that sound deep
rules.guidance: Replace unsupported aphorisms or revelations with the specific mechanism, relationship or claim. Inspect metaphors beyond the watch list semantically.
rules.exceptions: Keep literal scientific terms, a precise theoretical definition, an attributed quotation, or a necessary contrast. The architecture of a network is not automatically an aphorism.

rules.title: Staged run-up before the point
rules.guidance: Begin with the scientific point instead of announcing an explanation or staging candor.
rules.exceptions: Do not rewrite code, quoted interview speech, source titles or genuine first-person statements that are part of the data.

rules.title: Arguing with no one
rules.guidance: Check whether the objection or rejected option actually belongs to the argument or reader context; express any remaining substantive claim directly.
rules.exceptions: Retain an attributed reviewer objection, a scientifically important alternative explanation, a documented limitation, or a real decision alternative.

rules.title: Forced triads
rules.guidance: Review three-part lists and three parallel examples at sentence and paragraph scales. Each item must add a distinct supported idea; do not compress away a condition or outcome.
rules.exceptions: Keep three actual datasets, measurements, assumptions, treatment groups or other distinct real items. Counting three items cannot establish a forced rhetorical triad.

rules.title: Repeated sentence openings
rules.guidance: Inspect adjacent repeated subjects/openings and rewrite paragraph structure when repetition is mechanical, without changing actor or agency.
rules.exceptions: Intentional parallel definitions, enumerated results, quotations and deliberate rhetoric can legitimately repeat an opening.

rules.title: Dashes as the universal connector
rules.guidance: For ordinary prose without a writing sample, replace dash connectors only after choosing the real clause relation. A supplied sample overrides the general punctuation preference.
rules.exceptions: Preserve numerical ranges, minus signs, names such as Mann–Whitney, scientific terminology, code, commands, paths, URLs and quoted words. Scientific notation takes priority over blanket dash removal.

rules.title: Stacked qualifiers
rules.guidance: Review stacked uncertainty language and retain the qualifier, scope and source of uncertainty actually supported by the evidence.
rules.exceptions: A real uncertainty statement, a necessary inference label, legal/safety notice or correction is not clutter. Never make an empirical claim more certain to satisfy this rule.

rules.title: Hyphenated pairs everywhere
rules.guidance: Review unnecessary hyphens in predicate compounds; retain pre-noun compound modifiers and dictionary/venue-required spellings.
rules.exceptions: Keep established technical compounds, third-party, cross-functional, lexical spellings, minus signs, paths, commands and citations.

rules.title: Passive voice and missing subjects
rules.guidance: Review missing agency when active wording would clarify who performed an action. Recover an actor only from an actual source.
rules.exceptions: Scientific methods often use legitimate passive voice, especially when the actor is irrelevant or explicitly identified. Do not invent an experimenter or turn an unknown actor into 'we'.

rules.title: Overused AI words
rules.guidance: Inspect word clusters and rhetorical function, not just vocabulary. Prefer a precise domain term or measured claim over ornamental repetition.
rules.exceptions: Technical robust regression, key variables/keys, physical or logic gates, energy/fitness landscapes and literal uses are legitimate. A word's presence is neither authorship evidence nor sufficient reason to change terminology.

rules.title: Inflated significance
rules.guidance: Inspect inflated phrases, stock challenges/outlook sections and send-off paragraphs. Keep concrete findings and documented future plans rather than invented significance.
rules.exceptions: Preserve a source-supported historical consequence, justified clinical relevance, preregistered practical significance, or specific future experiment.

rules.title: Vague connection or association
rules.guidance: Name the relationship only when the source establishes it. Otherwise preserve the actual uncertainty rather than inventing a role, mechanism or causal link.
rules.exceptions: Statistical association is a necessary scientific term; retain observational association, confidence intervals, adjusted effects and noncausal interpretation. Never change 'associated with' into 'causes'.

rules.title: Shallow -ing riders
rules.guidance: Check whether the trailing participial interpretation follows from the cited observation; retain supported mechanism or consequence and remove only unsupported evaluation.
rules.exceptions: A measured or source-supported mechanism, mathematically established implication or necessary causal condition is substantive.

rules.title: Sales language
rules.guidance: Replace promotional valuation with what was measured, compared, implemented or documented.
rules.exceptions: Preserve proper names, quoted data and literal scientific terms such as nutrient-rich medium; do not invent a quantitative replacement for an unsupported adjective.

rules.title: Borrowed authority
rules.guidance: Distinguish an exact source and its claim from unnamed experts, prestige-outlet lists or popularity. Keep actual attributable evidence; never invent an expert or citation.
rules.exceptions: A properly attributed systematic review, bibliometric measurement, actual named quotation or study of media coverage can legitimately discuss authority and attention.

rules.title: Avoiding is, are, and has
rules.guidance: Use simple copulas when the longer verb adds no meaning. Verify the original relationship before replacing a functional, temporal or technical verb.
rules.exceptions: A functional role, dynamic process, named mathematical representation, defined reference or maintained invariant may require the longer verb.

rules.title: Bold as decoration
rules.guidance: Review repeated bold labels/colons and indiscriminate emphasis in raw formatting. Convert a list only when no label, condition, ranking or item-specific fact is lost.
rules.exceptions: Venue-required headings, defined terms, tensor/vector math, accessibility emphasis, quoted formatting and structured reporting checklists may require bold.

rules.title: Decorative headings
rules.guidance: Review title case, decorative heading/list emojis or arrows, repeated horizontal rules and a heading duplicating the document title. Use the real section subject and the required venue format.
rules.exceptions: Preserve scientific acronyms, proper names, mathematical arrows, required title case, template separators and labels with real meaning.

rules.title: Curly quotation marks
rules.guidance: Check the actual target-format convention or writing sample before recommending straight versus curly quotation marks; automatic editor typography alone is weak evidence.
rules.exceptions: Keep exact quoted words, apostrophes, primes in scientific notation, source/code text and the venue's typography. This rule never licenses altering a quoted claim.

rules.title: Chatbot residue
rules.guidance: Remove interactional wrappers from the manuscript while retaining the actual scientific content.
rules.exceptions: Keep interview quotations, chatbot-output study data, titles, legitimate correspondence salutations/sign-offs and passages discussing these phrases.

rules.title: Knowledge-limit disclaimers and guesses
rules.guidance: Remove model-knowledge boilerplate and unsupported guesses. State a real source gap without filling it with a plausible invented biography or fact.
rules.exceptions: A dated search cutoff, data freeze, explicit source-coverage limit, genuine unavailability statement or bounded scientific uncertainty is necessary evidence metadata.

rules.title: A heading repeated in the first sentence
rules.guidance: Check the first paragraph after a heading for a redundant restatement, including semantic paraphrases with different words.
rules.exceptions: Keep a first sentence that adds a definition, result, scope restriction, study population or other new information. Lexical overlap alone cannot establish redundancy.

rules.title: Writing about the document instead of its subject
rules.guidance: Remove obvious layout narration or editing history when it adds nothing to the scientific subject; state a necessary convention once.
rules.exceptions: Retain actual Methods/provenance, source credits, data-generation procedures, cross-references required to locate results, change logs and response-to-reviewer commitments.

rules.title: Re-explaining what the reader knows
rules.guidance: Apply only to a reply with surrounding conversation or an explicitly known reader. Lead with the decision and retain reasoning that affects it; compare background with what the reader already supplied.
rules.exceptions: A scientific introduction, standalone paper, new collaborator or unknown readership may need background. Without surrounding context, request review instead of deleting information.
